title: Sharp Threshold for Transitive Increasing Boolean Functions
statement: There is a constant $B>0$ such that for every $n\ge2$ and every increasing, transitively symmetric function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ that is nonconstant, suppose $p_c,\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<p_c\le\tfrac12$, the biased probability that $f=1$ at $p_c$ is $\tfrac12$, and $0<\varepsilon<\tfrac14$. Set $\displaystyle\eta=B\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)\log(1/p_c)}{\log n}$. If $\eta\le\tfrac12$, then the biased probability that $f=1$ at $p_c(1-\eta)$ is at most $\varepsilon$, and at $p_c(1+\eta)$ it is at least $1-\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is transitively symmetric under coordinate permutations
The biased probability that $f=1$ at $p_c$ equals $\tfrac12$
replaced: There exists an absolute $B>0$ such that for every $n\ge2$, nonconstant increasing transitively symmetric $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, $0<p_c\le1/2$ with $\Pr_{p_c}(f=1)=1/2$, and $0<\varepsilon<1/4$, the number $\eta=B\log(1/\varepsilon)\log(1/p_c)/\log n$ satisfies: if $\eta\le1/2$, then $\Pr_{p_c(1-\eta)}(f=1)\le\varepsilon$ and $\Pr_{p_c(1+\eta)}(f=1)\ge1-\varepsilon$.
